subject: ENTRY-CONVENTION clause
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 11.9.7.4 "The ENTRY-CONVENTION clause specifies the convention to be used for activating the runtime element" -> OK GR1). The implementation provides exactly one convention (COBOL = the uniform ICobolProgram.Call ABI, DOC-A.1-64); the clause is accepted in every SR1-permitted element and a non-COBOL name is refused rather than silently mapped (PB232 landed). Probed: outermost program (p1), function definition activated via REPOSITORY FUNCTION (p2 prints 'P2 042'), program prototype + function prototype (p3), class (p4, methods invoked), interface (p5, p6) -- all accept and run; method/FACTORY/OBJECT placement refused COBOL2385 (n1). With one convention there is nothing to select, so the clause has no model field: OptionsBinder.ScreenEntryConvention applies SR1 and GR3 and nothing else reads the clause, and the program is activated with the COBOL convention (kb/Work PB298 deleted the producer-only OptionsModel.EntryConvention; OptionsModelConsumerDriftTests refuses an OPTIONS model field that has no consumer). || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 2014, 2023 (the 2023 Annex E lists no introduction or change of the clause, so it predates 2023; whether ISO 1989:2002 carried it is not derivable from specs/ISO_COBOL.md -- the code gates it 2014 as a recorded conservative choice, constructs.json options-entry-convention-2014) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/OptionsBinder.cs#EntryConventionOf (kb/Work PB298: the ENTRY-CONVENTION screen returns nothing now that the clause has no model field, so EntryConventionOf became ScreenEntryConvention (the same SR1 + GR3 checks, COBOL2385); kb/Work PB298: OptionsModel.EntryConvention was read by nobody (the screen admits only COBOL, the implied convention of GR4 c), so the field is deleted; OptionsModelConsumerDriftTests keeps a producer-only OPTIONS field out) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/OptionsModel.cs#EntryConvention (kb/Work PB298: the ENTRY-CONVENTION screen returns nothing now that the clause has no model field, so EntryConventionOf became ScreenEntryConvention (the same SR1 + GR3 checks, COBOL2385); kb/Work PB298: OptionsModel.EntryConvention was read by nobody (the screen admits only COBOL, the implied convention of GR4 c), so the field is deleted; OptionsModelConsumerDriftTests keeps a producer-only OPTIONS field out)
